moduleTitle: Lesson 7 - Building Your First Mobile TestCase
learningObjectives: Open a native/hybrid app after any required Desired Capabilities setup, and distinguish mobile website opening.
Use the core gesture Modules — Click, Swipe, and Draw On Screen — for coordinate-based interaction.
Enter text into mobile controls and control keyboard autohide behaviour.
Run and observe a mobile TestCase using LiveView.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Opening the application after capability setup

elements.description: Use Open Mobile App to begin native/hybrid application steering. Desired Capabilities setup is the documented exception: Set Desired Capabilities, and any additions, precede application opening. Mobile websites use OpenUrl.

elements.text: Do not generalize this ordering to every Engine or resource-opening Module. Check the specific application and capability workflow.

elements.term: What Open Mobile App actually does
elements.description: It's more than a click-through step: Open Mobile App creates the mobile device session (via TMA) for the TestCase, and it can install the app on the device at the start of that session if an install source (a local .apk path, or the equivalent iOS install path) is configured — or, for an app already on the device, open it directly by its identifier: BundleID for iOS, or AppPackage/AppActivity for Android.

For TestCases that move between apps mid-flow (e.g. testing a deep link handoff, or a share-sheet interaction that opens a different app), Switch Mobile App changes the active app context without needing a second Open Mobile App step.

bulletPoints: Native/hybrid opening follows any required Desired Capabilities setup.
Switch Mobile App selects another app during the TestCase.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Gestures: when there's no control to click

elements.title: Coordinate-based interaction Modules
items: Click On Screen — taps a specific x/y coordinate rather than a scanned control, for spots the scan couldn't identify as a distinct element.
Swipe On Screen — supports directional swipes or SWIPE with configured start/end points.
Draw On Screen — a free-form drawing/path gesture, used for things like signature capture or gesture-based unlock patterns.

elements.text: Coordinates need validation against the actual layout. Click/Swipe support percentages as well as pixels; relative coordinates can scale with the screen but do not automatically locate a moved control. Prefer stable scanned identifiers when suitable.

bulletPoints: Click/Swipe can use relative percentages or pixels; Draw uses percentage points.
Coordinates do not guarantee control identity across changed layouts.

elements.term: Send Text Input To Focused Control
elements.description: Enters text into whichever control currently has focus — typically used right after tapping a text field, mirroring how a real user would tap then type.

Set Autohide Keyboard controls iOS onscreen keyboard auto-hide: True enables it and False disables it. Check the actual platform and resulting keyboard state; do not present this as a universal Android/iOS dismissal guarantee.

bulletPoints: Tap the field, then Send Text Input To Focused Control — mirrors real user behaviour.
Configure iOS auto-hide where appropriate and verify that the next target is accessible.

elements.description: For local mobile execution, LiveView=True displays a screenshot preview when the TestStep changes. It is not a continuous video or proof of the exact screen at every failure instant.

elements.text: Use preview alongside execution logs and assertions during debugging. Choose preview settings for the run’s needs rather than assuming a measured performance improvement from switching it off.

bulletPoints: Live View previews local execution at TestStep changes.
Use execution logs and assertions to validate failures and outcomes.

examPitfalls.title: Steering before application opening or omitting capability setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding navigation or verification TestSteps before the Open Mobile App Module.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Place required Desired Capabilities configuration before Open Mobile App for native/hybrid apps. Mobile websites use their OpenUrl workflow.

examPitfalls.title: Reaching for On Screen gestures as a default
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using Click On Screen with hardcoded coordinates for a control that was actually captured and addressable during scanning.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Prefer useful scanned identifiers. Relative coordinates scale with screen dimensions but still require layout validation; pixel coordinates add resolution sensitivity.

examPitfalls.title: Not accounting for the on-screen keyboard
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A TestStep intermittently fails to tap an element that's actually being covered by the still-open keyboard from the previous text-entry step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: On iOS, configure auto-hide appropriately and verify the actual keyboard state. Use platform-appropriate handling rather than assuming a universal Module hides every keyboard.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For a native/hybrid TestCase that does not first set Desired Capabilities, which Module opens the application before steering?

options.text: Connect to Mobile Agent
Open Mobile App
Mobile Scan
Any Module — the order is unconstrained.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario excludes the documented capabilities-first exception.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Open Mobile App opens native/hybrid apps. Required Desired Capabilities steps can precede it; mobile websites have an OpenUrl workflow.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the documented app-opening Module.
optionExplanations.B: This opens the native/hybrid app under the stated ordering.
optionExplanations.C: Mobile Scan creates Modules rather than opening the TestCase application.
optionExplanations.D: Application opening and capability setup constrain the order.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When a target has no useful scanned identifier, how should the team evaluate Click On Screen?

options.text: Always — it's simpler than dealing with scanned control properties.
As a coordinate-based alternative, validating percentage or pixel positions against the target layout.
Only on iOS, never on Android.
Only inside a hybrid app's webview context.

practiceQuiz.hint: Coordinates are a fallback, not a default choice.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Coordinates can provide an alternative, but they identify positions rather than stable control identity. Percentages scale with the screen; they do not guarantee a moved element remains at that position.

optionExplanations.A: Position-based steering needs validation rather than universal use.
optionExplanations.B: Validate the configured position against the actual layout.
optionExplanations.C: This is not an iOS-only interaction.
optionExplanations.D: It is not limited to hybrid webviews.

practiceQuiz.scenario: On iOS, the keyboard visibly covers the next target after text entry. Which issue should the team address?

options.text: The button's resource-id changed between runs.
The on-screen keyboard is still open and covering the button.
TMA lost connection to the device.
The TestCase needs an Open Mobile App step added.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what's still on screen right after typing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario confirms the obstruction. Check the iOS keyboard auto-hide configuration and actual dismissal rather than inferring a connection or identifier failure.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario confirms obstruction rather than an identifier change.
optionExplanations.B: The keyboard visibly covers the intended target.
optionExplanations.C: The supplied evidence does not establish a lost connection.
optionExplanations.D: Adding another open step does not address the confirmed obstruction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does Switch Mobile App allow a TestCase to do?

options.text: Restart the currently open app from scratch.
Change the active app context mid-TestCase, for flows that legitimately span two apps.
Switch between Local and Remote TMA connections.
Toggle LiveView on and off during execution.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about app context, not connection topology.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Switch Mobile App changes the active app context mid-TestCase — for example testing a deep link or a share-sheet handoff — without a second Open Mobile App step.

optionExplanations.A: Switching apps is not a guaranteed full reset.
optionExplanations.B: It changes the selected application during the TestCase.
optionExplanations.C: It does not change the connection topology.
optionExplanations.D: It does not configure Live View.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statements are true about "Open Mobile App" in Tosca Mobile? (three correct answers)

options.text: Creates mobile device sessions
Requires its Android AppActivity field when switching to every installed iOS app
Enables the installation of apps at the start of the test session with Tricentis Mobile Agent
Opens already installed apps by defining bundle IDs for iOS apps or package and activity names for Android apps

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish supported opening methods from a wrong platform-specific field.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Module can create the session, install a supplied app build, or open an installed app with the platform’s identifiers. Android AppActivity is not required for installed iOS apps; Open Mobile App does support native and hybrid applications.

optionExplanations.A: The app-opening workflow establishes a mobile session.
optionExplanations.B: Android AppActivity is not required to select an installed iOS application.
optionExplanations.C: A configured installation path can supply a target-compatible app build.
optionExplanations.D: These are the platform-specific installed application identifiers.

quickRecap.value: Open native/hybrid apps after required capability setup; websites use OpenUrl.
Select another app by its platform identifier during the TestCase.
Validate coordinate gestures; percentages scale with screen dimensions but do not identify moved controls.
Set focus before Send Text Input To Focused Control.
Set Autohide Keyboard controls iOS auto-hide; verify the resulting keyboard state.
LiveView=True gives local TestStep-change previews, not continuous video or exact failure snapshots.
